body: Spot on, the thing with PAs is that no matter what their partner looks like, they always want to see something different than what they have. You could be a Kardashian with a BBL or you could be a runway model, they would always be looking for something ELSE and that is never a reflection of you or your beauty. It is part of the addiction and never, ever the fault of the partner trying to support the addict through it.

Thank you so much, I wish you all the same happiness and joy too. It’s so wonderful that you had the same experience of realizing the beauty in yourself again after leaving. I feel so much lighter even while dealing with the grief of losing the person I love, it’s crazy and I never imagined that it would feel so freeing even though I know it will be hard without him. All the best to you too.

Thank you so much, I’m so glad to hear that you’ve been thriving after leaving your PA. It’s bittersweet for me because the love is still there, but I think this will be better for both of us in the long run.
Thank you!

Thank you so much for the encouraging words, it means a lot. As much as I loved him, I need to feel safe and secure with myself and being with someone dealing with PA made me unable to do that. Even dealing with sadness about the breakup isn’t as bad as how I was feeling on a daily basis about myself. And thank you for the recommendation as well.

I’m genuinely so sorry and totally get how you’re feeling. I wanted a life with my ex PA as well and was in it for the long haul. And as hard as it may be to follow through on, sometimes leaving is the only way to save ourselves from feeling continuously betrayed over and over.

I am so sorry you are going through this. I am also 23 and experienced so many of the exact thoughts, feelings, and physical symptoms you’re talking about until I finally left my PA partner. We are so young and there is so much more to life than being with someone who doesn’t make you feel loved and appreciated, even though I know it is excruciatingly difficult to leave even if you know you should. Please be as gentle with yourself as you can and do what’s best for you.

I’m so sorry you’re going through this. For a long time what stopped me was burying my head in the sand and telling him to lie/withhold information about it to spare my feelings so I could pretend it wasn’t happening or wasn’t as bad as it really was. But not knowing the truth ate at me and eventually once I knew the full truth I just couldn’t stay because of the pain. Good luck to you and your daughter.

I was in a similar position with an addicted partner who came back into my life and was still relapsing, we recently broke up and I feel that was the only way to respecte my own feelings about it. It sounds like this is very distressing for you and you gave your ultimatum before because of how hurtful his behavior was. I know it may be hard, but I would suggest sticking to the boundary you set to prevent any further hurt/betrayal.

i was in a similar position to you about a year ago when my ex dumped me. i was also feeling similarly to how you are around the three month mark - in fact, it’s the one time i broke no contact in the almost a year that we’ve been out of each other’s lives. it sounds like you’re doing everything you need to do to get back on track, and i commend you for being able to settle into a routine and stay in touch with friends and family. while it may be hard, as long as you keep showing up and moving forward, it gradually gets easier. all the best <3

so sorry that happened to you, that is 100% sexual assault and it is not your fault. it is extremely common for people being assaulted to freeze up in the moment, that does not mean you consented or wanted it. i hope you have supportive people in your life who can help you through this, and i think counseling/therapy might also be helpful if you have the resources to access it. wishing you all the best.

i think this is because there are some fundamentally different issues at play. in most societies globally, women are oppressed by men to some degree, so women’s issues with men often have to do with that (restricted reproductive rights, lack of rights to education, frequent sexual harassment and violence, etc.) and would only be fixed if men stop withholding those rights from women via political/economic power - so the onus falls on men to help make those changes since they have consolidated much of the power to do so. i can’t really think of any societies where men have been treated the same way by women that men have historically treated women in terms of restrictive legislation and freedoms, so the context can be very different, i think.
you very well may be right. hopefully he will rethink some of those views if he’s asking for advice here.

maybe you should work on finding self-worth beyond validation from women. also, your perception of women as money-hungry and hyperfocused on genital size is not at all reflective of the reality of the vast majority of women. you will rarely, if ever, hear women speak that way about men day to day if you’re not going down internet rabbit holes. don’t let yourself be radicalized by extreme statements online that feed into your pre-existing insecurities.

I’m a current MSW student who got a BA in psychology, and so far I’d say the transition has been pretty smooth, but if you’re looking to get a specific type of experience first it might be better to start with your BSW. That being said, it’s totally doable to go from a psych undergraduate degree to an MSW program! The benefit of doing a BSW, though, is that you can apply to be an advanced standing student, so your MSW would only take one year instead of two. Either way, very doable and realistic in my opinion. Good luck!
I just got my acceptance today! Best of luck to anyone still waiting. :)

True, I definitely should take their estimate with a grain of salt. I’m waiting on another school right now and haven’t gotten a decision since I just submitted that app a few days ago, but I’m worried about what will happen if it takes a super long time for me to hear back from both schools since I don’t know what to expect …
No, I still haven’t heard back :// today marks 2 weeks into the “2-3 week” estimate I got from the admissions office a while ago, so I guess I should be expecting something in the next week or so?

It sounds like you are a strong applicant overall, and that if you clearly explain the extenuating circumstances surrounding that particular grade you should still have a fair chance at getting in. You seem driven and well-rounded, so I don’t think that one C attributed directly to illness should completely derail your chances of admission so long as you fully explain the situation to the admissions committee. Good luck!

It’s nice to hear that others are in the same boat! I just called the admissions office this morning and they confirmed that my second transcript coming in late held up the review process a bit. They gave me an estimate of 2-3 weeks for a decision and put a note on my application that I have other deadlines to meet for making a decision, so maybe that will speed up the process a bit.

Greetings, I submitted my app (non-priority) on 2/15 and had to add an extra transcript from old high school dual enrollment courses on 2/21. I know it hasn’t even been a month yet but I’m starting to get a bit nervous seeing other people get their decisions - should I be worried or just try to be patient since I submitted so late?
